title: A9 motorway: car strikes stopped van
location_guess: A9 motorway near Munich, Germany (TUM Traffic gantry cameras)
summary: First 32 seconds at 12.5 fps. Calibrated crash-side trajectories, asymmetric measured lane lines and fixed median geometry. 139 background tracks; background visibility follows audited source spans.

views.description: Bottom-right crash camera; calibrated 479x300 tile, crop x=481 y=304; 12.5 fps.

crash.kind: car strikes stopped van near median verge
crash.description: Frame-timed contacts from crash_pair.json. Inferred geometry and impulses are labeled individually. Moving or out-of-view vehicles are not assumed to be at rest.

contacts.note: Footprint first crosses the measured soft-verge edge, supported by paint/wheel silhouette at the snow/asphalt boundary. Timing +/-2 frames; this is verge encroachment, not proof of a rigid hedge/barrier impact. Static impulse is unidentifiable and is intentionally omitted. Steering, sliding and soft-ground resistance cannot be separated from this view.

First supported rear/median-side-corner contact f291; physical touch is hidden by the van and bounded to f290-292. Van rocks at f292 then translates clearly at f293. Impulse is van mass times fitted post-impact longitudinal velocity over f296-300, including unresolved tyre forces; mass is assumed.

static_objects.label: median verge (snow-covered grass)
static_objects.note: At the crash site (X 56-159 m) the median is a vegetated verge: plowed snow on grass from the crash-side edge Y=-8.64 to Y=-6.94, bare grass to the far-side barrier (lit face foot Y=-4.72, right-carriageway side). No tall hedge/barrier is visible on the crash side. A low kerb or asphalt/verge lip is unresolved: the painted edge line (calibrated Y=-9.03) and ~0.26 m of asphalt are visible next to it, which bounds the verge height at its crash-side edge to <= 0.33 m; the height of the snow-covered vegetation itself is not resolvable from this single fixed view (height_m 0.15 is an estimate, height_sigma_m 0.15). Beyond X=159 m the verge ends and the median is paved, bordered on the crash side by a dark band (see related_objects: median-hedge-far). No tall 'bushy' hedge is visible next to the crash site itself: a vehicle leaving lane 1 to its left runs onto this soft verge first and reaches the barrier ~3.6 m further on. assumed (typical values for the material); not measured

static_objects.label: median barrier (far side)
static_objects.note: Bright band Y -4.90..-4.72 on the road plane along the whole visible median (calibration line R_barrier Y=-4.80 is its centre). Read as the lit right-carriageway face of a barrier with its foot at Y=-4.72; the projected width gives height ~0.54 m (sigma 0.2). Thickness 0.3 m is assumed (the median-side face is hidden). Concrete vs steel is not resolvable at this resolution. assumed (typical values for the material); not measured

static_objects.label: median hedge band (far section)
static_objects.note: Dark band Y -8.85..-7.69 (road-plane projection) on the crash side of the paved median beyond X=159 m; saturation 20 vs asphalt 4 and paved median 15: vegetation-like, probably a low hedge (could be a barrier in shade). Height assumed 0.5 m; its crash-side face is then at Y=-8.45. Far from the crash site (X~80 m). assumed (typical values for the material); not measured

caveats: Frame measurements use a calibrated pinhole camera; dash spacing and assumed van width set scale. Uncertainty is retained per sample.
Measured road has 6 crash-side strips and 3 opposing strips; no symmetric lane fit or lateral shift.

Background visibility follows the supplied audited measured/interpolated spans. Run-in/run-out identity outside those spans is unknown; a track can first appear inside the image where its first reliable fit occurs.

Manual lane census retains residual differences: inferred/occluded tracks can remain without a visible source body, and horizon/edge identities are uncertain. Complete one-to-one visible-traffic coverage has not been established.

The crash-side median near the crash is a low snow-covered verge, separate from its far-side barrier and the uncertain far-section hedge band. Heights and contact parameters are estimates; see static-object notes.
Contact times/points, normals and impulses retain their inferred/measured labels; forces derived from fitted motion are not instrumented.
Vehicle dimensions are clamped to viewer class ranges; pedestrians and debris are omitted.
Source: demo_32s.mp4, frames 0..399, 12.5 fps, exact bottom-right crop (481,304,479,300), cam.py/calib_joint.json. All coordinates, vectors and contact normals here are W.

Yellow-car first reliable identity is f151 (12.08 s), initially in lane 1. It is a tiny unlabelled light vehicle in earlier distant frames, but a unique association before f151 cannot be established from this crop; the actual first in-view frame remains unresolved. No invented approach is added for f0-150. f151-154 are labelled interpolated because the first box is partially occluded/tiny.

Agreement with the user: the identified yellow car approaches in lane 1, moves outward into lane 2, then turns sharply back toward lane 1/median and rotates before hitting the van rear/median-side corner. It does not follow a straight lane-2 approach throughout the clip.

Qualified agreement: the outward manoeuvre passes alongside slower traffic, consistent with overtaking, but driver intent cannot be observed. A large outward-then-inward lateral swing and body rotation are clear. Repeated small wiggles before that swing are not resolved and have not been fabricated.

The van is stationary at (80.564,-10.368) in lane 1 next to the median, through f290. Its constant pose was fitted to visible ground/top box corners, not an assumed lane centre. Small pre-impact raw fit drift is rasterisation/occlusion noise.

First supported vehicle contact is f291 (23.28 s); hidden physical touch may fall in f290-292. Van body rocks at f292 and moves forward unmistakably by f293. The prior fallback 22.3 s contact is contradicted.

The van travels about 18 m toward the camera and slightly outward, then stops near f353. It remains partially visible at the lower-left border through f399. No out-of-view van extrapolation is necessary; clipped pose uncertainty is larger.

Yellow paint/side silhouette remains measurable beside the van through f316. f317-318 interpolate the last occluded turn. f319-399 hold the final constrained region behind the van with src=occluded-rest and sigma growing from 3 to 5 m. The exact resting pose/time is NOT directly measured. Continued hidden motion cannot be excluded; this retention avoids disappearance without inventing an unobserved path.

W3 divider.json was checked: median-divider is a snow-covered grass verge, crash-side face Y=-8.637, X=55.5..158.875. The far-side median-barrier face is Y=-5.025. Yellow footprint/silhouette reaches the soft verge before vehicle contact. No yellow-car/far-barrier contact and no van/divider contact are supported; no such contacts are emitted.

Body heading during the spin uses visible bonnet/window/side silhouette to resolve the 180-degree cuboid ambiguity. Sparse frame-checked controls, interpolated frames, and the approximate final hidden heading retain 1.2-5 m position uncertainty; precise yaw is less certain than vehicle presence.

The car f291 pose is contact-constrained within the roughly 1.2 m visual position uncertainty; the actual touching surfaces are hidden. It is labelled interpolated, not an independently measured contact pose. Body heading can remain uncertain by roughly 20-40 degrees in the partially occluded spin.

Van dimensions are the calibration cuboid (5.054 x 2.05 x 2.657 m). Yellow dimensions 4.3 x 1.8 x 1.5 m are class priors constrained by its unoccluded box, with roughly 0.5 m length/0.15 m width uncertainty. Masses 1350 and 2500 kg are assumptions, not video measurements; forces/impulses scale linearly with these masses.

Velocity and acceleration are finite differences of the delivered frame positions; planar force equals assumed mass times acceleration. Cause labels describe the observed phase, not a measured decomposition of tyre, verge and body-contact forces. Impact impulses and peak forces are model-dependent, not sensor readings.

The flat-plane camera is calibrated best at X<335 m. Early yellow-car poses extend beyond that range; at X~540 m one image row is about 16 m. Their sigma reflects this weak depth/grade constraint. Do not interpret those early acceleration fluctuations as braking events.

Background initial velocity prior vx=-18 +/-18 m/s (1 sigma), vy=0 +/-2 m/s; horizon slopes are not independent physical speed measurements. sigma_v_mps is conditional smoother uncertainty and excludes identity/calibration error. Raw fitted positions and simultaneous alternatives remain in tracks_px_clean.json. No manufactured vehicles or speed caps.

Tracking audit: Visible source gaps remain. A large unboxed dark/brown truck approaches through the background (clear at f250/f300/f350/f399; partly clipped at f212/f213). The wireframe-based detector does not establish a complete independent track for it. The clipped left-edge car slivers at f212 and f399 have no secure delivered identity. No path was manufactured to fill these gaps. See the corresponding primary manual marks/source images.

Tracking audit: Counts differ around 17s. At f212 there are 31 delivered bodies versus 26 primary source marks, including six inferred tracks. At f213 there are 31 versus 25, including four inferred tracks. This is not a passing lane-coverage result. Inferred c084/c092 near a truck, c026/c094 source component associations and c050/c086 around occlusion remain ambiguous; some may be retained fragments of one physical vehicle. They were not merged without sufficiently clear source identity evidence.

Tracking audit: The end-of-clip visible deficit remains. f399 gives 22 delivered versus 24 primary source marks, while the delivered set includes the hidden yellow wreck. Its measured-visible count is 21. Horizon separability/lane uncertainty affects the exact deficit; total subtraction alone cannot identify all missing vehicles. f350 likewise includes the hidden wreck despite equal primary totals.

Tracking audit: Near-horizon class, size, speed and lane assignments remain provisional. Some fits use only one face or a colored annotation component. No same-class scan or subpixel reprojection score validates their physical identity. c166 is a short horizon example with weak derivative information. Generic projected straight outer lanes also make L6/L7 assignment uncertain.

Tracking audit: Crash-pair limits are preserved. Yellow identity before f151 remains unresolved; no early path was invented. Its f319–399 hidden resting pose is inferred with increased uncertainty. W2 collision/rest/heading caveats remain authoritative. No new collision, queue, pile-up or immovable-object conclusion was inferred here.
